text:
cheng: Heads-up — canary of the continuous-batching refactor is showing a degradation for streamed responses. Not huge, but p95 latency up ~30% and CPU jitter increased. attaching quick profiler excerpt and notes.

raj: repro steps? which flags changed in canary?

cheng: quick notes: we switched to adaptive flush (tries to avoid empty flushes) + token_budget_target tuned to 12 from 16. Also partial-decode scheduling now preempts earlier to favor low latency. Repro on local canary: small prompt fanout (avg seq 48), many concurrent short streams (~500 qps).

maria: do you have KV cache stats? my hunch: partial decode preemption may be causing extra KV copy/evictions for streamed clients.

cheng: yep — KV numbers look suspicious. profiler:
```
[perf] canary=cb-refactor-3 model=rw-7b-sv qps=520 p50_stream=24ms p95_stream=220ms p95_nonstream=95ms
KernelSelect: preferred=int8 qps_target=600 -> fallback=fp16 path for many slices
KVCache: resident_mb=4380 miss_ratio=0.42 (was 0.11 on baseline)
Scheduler: avg_batch_size=6 -> 4.1 after adaptive flush
```

sam: miss_ratio 0.42 is huge. if batch size dropped it's expected perf hit. adaptive flush probably too eager for streams. what are flush thresholds?

cheng: current canary config excerpt:
```
continuous_batching:
  max_latency_ms: 10
  token_budget_target: 12
  flush_mode: adaptive
  partial_decode_preempt_ms: 6
  allow_small_batches: true
```

olivia: partial_decode_preempt_ms=6 might be preempting useful batching. Streams with early partial decodes keep flushing and avoid building stable KV windows. Could cause kernel re-selection thrash because sequence lengths change mid-batch.

raj: kernel re-selection thrash? explain.

maria: when batches shrink, kernel choice sometimes flips from int8 fast path to fp16 fallback because quantization heuristics use avg_seq and present_kv_size heuristics. Frequent flips cause more memory copies and context rebinds -> CPU overhead and higher p95.

perf-bot: perf alert: canary cb-refactor-3 p95_stream +32% over baseline for 3 consecutive 5m windows :eyes:

sam: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) increase token_budget_target to 16 to allow slightly larger batches for streams, 2) raise min_flush_ms to avoid tiny-batch flushes, 3) tweak partial_decode_preempt to be less aggressive (e.g., 12ms).

cheng: I ran a quick experiment on staging: token_budget_target=16 + min_flush_ms=8 => avg_batch_size went 6.1 and p95_stream dropped to 130ms (still above baseline but better). KV miss_ratio down to 0.18. so looks promising.

olivia: nice. we should also consider a guard in the scheduler: if request is stream and partial_decode requested, prefer to schedule it at end of current batch rather than preempting current batch. that preserves KV continuity.

raj: could add per-client KV affinity window too — keep same worker if KV present, avoid repopulating. That's more infra work though.

maria: for kernel selection, add hysteresis: require two consecutive evaluation windows to flip kernel path. avoids flip-flop when batch sizes bounce.

cheng: noted. quick config patch I want to try next:
```
continuous_batching:
  token_budget_target: 16
  min_flush_ms: 8
  partial_decode_preempt_ms: 12
  kernel_selection_hysteresis: 2
  stream_affinity_ms: 250
```

sam: looks good. can you run 24h A/B with canary vs patched? prefer run on same load shape with short-stream-heavy traffic.

cheng: yeah I'll kick it off. deploying patch to canary now. @deploy-bot canary push started.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: cb-refactor-3 -> cb-refactor-3a (patch). Canary subset: 3% traffic.

perf-bot: recommend adding KV hit/miss meter to the dashboard (stream vs non-stream breakdown) before we ramp.

olivia: +1 for dashboard. I'll add a short eval that simulates partial-decode preemption and measure KV churn.

raj: action items:
- cheng: run 24h A/B with patched config (token 16, min_flush_ms 8, preempt 12)
- olivia: add KV hit/miss per-stream metric + run synthetic eval
- maria: implement kernel_selection_hysteresis (low-risk change)
- sam: prepare rollback plan if canary worsens other traffic shapes

cheng: I'll post results in this thread when 3% -> 30% ramp finishes. thanks all :thumbsup:

(earlier note: I also attached a tiny flamegraph link in the real thread but omitted here — will paste in results post)
